title: Quota-first preference router with soft regional spillover
creator: Lina Zhang
description: Problem statement: Free and paid customers currently compete for the same serving lanes which causes noisy neighbor latency spikes and unpredictable cost for paid tiers. We need a routing layer that prefers paid/enterprise lanes for their requests while still allowing free-tier traffic to fall back into paid capacity when surplus exists, all within quota constraints and regional affinity expectations. Goal: implement a quota-aware preference router that enforces soft reservations for paid/enterprise plans, supports regional affinity, and performs graceful, observable spillover into fallback model variants when preferred lanes are saturated or quota-limited.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Requests from paid/enterprise plans are routed to 'reserved' lanes by default unless plan quota for that lane is exhausted.
2) Free-tier requests are routed to best-effort lanes; if idle capacity exists in paid lanes and policy permits, free requests may spill into paid lanes but are preemptible.
3) Regional affinity honored: requests should prefer same-region pools and only spill to another region after local capacity and quotas are exhausted.
4) When preferred model variant is unavailable, router picks the nearest compatible fallback variant (quantized/cheaper model) guided by a fallback matrix.
5) System exposes metrics for per-plan routing decisions, preemptions, quota consumption, and per-lane SLO violations.
6) Rollout can be toggled via feature flag and supports canary by tenant group.
7) End-to-end tests simulate quota exhaustion, regional outage, and verify correct demotion and preemption behavior.
design_decisions: Prefer soft reservations (credit buckets) over strict hard partitions to maximize utilization while preserving paid SLOs.
Use admission controller that checks (plan, tenant_credits, regional_capacity, model_compatibility) in that precedence order.
Fallback selection uses a scored compatibility table: (primary_model -> [variant, score, expected_latency, cost_delta]) maintained in configstore to avoid heavy logic in data plane.
Preemption: free-tier requests in paid lanes are tagged with eviction priority and displaced immediately when paid lane credits are claimed by higher-priority traffic.
Telemetry design favors sparse but high-signal events: preemption events, spillover counts, per-plan latency histograms, and quota imbalance alerts.
Regional spillover prefers same-cloud-region first, then nearest-region with cross-region penalty applied to score to avoid unnecessary ingress/egress costs.
We accepted the tradeoff of slightly increased decision CPU in exchange for fewer finger-pointing incidents and better paid-customer SLOs.
We will store small per-tenant credit counters in a consistent, low-latency KV (existing quota service) rather than replicating counters in the router to keep single source of truth.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API/Config): add config schema for plan priorities, soft-reserve credit thresholds, and fallback matrix entries.
Phase 2 (Router): implement QuotaCheck admission step: read tenant credits -> evaluate reservation eligibility -> assign lane tag and eviction policy.
Phase 3 (Regional logic): implement region preference with proximity penalty and fallback-to-region policy flags.
Phase 4 (Preemption): wire eviction signals from admission controller to in-flight request coordinator; implement immediate preempt for queued free requests.
Phase 5 (Observability): emit routing decision events and counters to tracing/metrics backend; create per-plan dashboards and alerts.
Phase 6 (Testing & Rollout): automated tests, canary on 5% of paid traffic, expand to 25%, monitor, then full rollout.
Estimated dev tasks: router logic (3), quota integration (2), telemetry (2), e2e tests (1).
rollout_plan: Gate behind feature flag `quota_preference_router_v1` adjustable per-tenant.
Canary strategy: start with internal tenants -> small set of low-risk paid customers -> ramp using automated health checks.
Fallback toggle that forces old routing path if preemption rate or paid SLO regressions exceed thresholds for 15m.
Communication: release notes to GTM and customer success describing behavior and expected temporary preemptions for free tier.
Post-rollout: run a 7-day observation window with a postmortem template for any SLO regressions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission logic and fallback scoring.
Integration tests with quota service simulator that exercises credit drains and replenishment windows.
Chaos test: simulate region outage and assert correct cross-region spillover and metrics generation.
Load test: synthetic mix of free/paid/enterprise traffic to validate preemption latency and throughput preservation for paid plans.
E2E test: tenant-level canary smoke that verifies no data-plane regressions and ensures model compatibility mapping is respected.
Observability validation: ensure traces include routing_reason, lane_id, preemption_flag, and fallback_variant tags.
metrics: Quota saturation events per tenant and per-lane
SLO breach count for paid plans (target: no increase > 1% during rollout)
links: Incident notes referencing related routing regressions: https://redwood.incidents/2025-11-routing-noisy-neighbor
